themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models again chose a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate, and audience caps, and the same pattern shows up as a single egress checkpoint in downstream consent and deletion, a shared pre-send eligibility check in cross-channel journey orchestration, and a declared-agent lane in governing agentic traffic.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often shifts while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable baseline because model outputs vary run to run, identity resolution has no way to verify matches outside the logged-in minority, cross-channel incrementality fights platforms that change the treatment mid-test, and generative content review cannot measure the mistakes reviewers never caught.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say proof stops at the perimeter and a trained model cannot forget one person without retraining, and on safe agent execution they note vendors expose neither agent identity nor any rollback, so containment has to be simulated from outside.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic work keeps failing because agents profit by looking human until a declared lane is genuinely better, journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for their own numbers, the semantic context layer is called a political settlement rather than a modeling gap, and ad supply integrity is blocked by parties who profit from unverified volume.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content review keeps returning to implied claims that no registry or classifier catches, the semantic context layer runs into terms that legitimately mean different things to different teams, and today's safe agent execution answer notes an agent following a poisoned instruction looks just like aggressive optimization until the money is gone.
